definition: Ecstatic means feeling or showing an intense, overpowering burst of joy, usually in reaction to specific news or a specific moment.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ecstatic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ecstatic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Theo was ecstatic when the shelter called: after eight months missing, his dog had wandered in that morning.
Glad is quiet, ordinary pleasure; ecstatic is joy erupting all at once, too big for the body to hold still.
Delirious pushes past even ecstatic — joy so overwhelming that clear thinking dissolves entirely.

Overjoyed means flooded with happiness, well past ordinary gladness. Ecstatic goes a step further: the joy is not just large but overpowering, bursting out of the body in screams, jumps, and hugs. A grandmother can be overjoyed at good news and still quietly finish her tea; an ecstatic person cannot sit still.

Thrilled means excited with a sudden rush of pleasure -- delighted, but still composed enough to carry on a conversation: a thrilled winner beams and says thank you. Ecstatic means the burst of joy has taken over completely, erupting in shouting or jumping. Thrilled stays inside the body; ecstatic pours out of it.

The minor-league dugout phone rang in the seventh inning.

The manager listened, hung up, and pointed at Delgado: "Pack your bag — the big club wants you tonight." Delgado dropped his glove, screamed, hugged three teammates at once, and tried to put his warm-up jacket on upside down.
Ten years of bus rides detonated into one ecstatic minute.
The scream, the tangled jacket, and the pile of hugs — an explosive reaction detonating in a single minute after specific news — show the sudden, overpowering burst of joy that ecstatic names.
vivid, everyday-to-literary; a reaction word

Ecstatic is a sudden, intense burst of joy tied to one specific piece of news or one moment, while euphoric (also in this unit) is the sustained, dreamlike high that can float on for days afterward — the acceptance call makes you ecstatic; the week that follows is euphoric.

When she finally read the first line, the quiet lasted about two seconds.
She was ecstatic — she screamed loud enough to bring her brother running from the yard, then danced the envelope around the kitchen like a trophy.
